quote: requested the info from T and M.
stewart_read: Customer references a prior request from what sounds like another source (T-Mobile or similar); rep never asks what that was or clarifies the lead's origin.
alternative_hypothesis: The audio/diarization is unclear and 'T and M' may be a mishearing of Ion or another internal term, so the rep may have correctly judged it wasn't worth pursuing.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always ask 'what's T&M?' or similar when a customer references a prior contact/source by name — even a 5-second clarifying question建立 competitive context for the closer.

quote: Yes. Okay. So we have a program. It's called the bill swap.
stewart_read: Customer asks 'How does it work?' and the rep answers with the standard bill-swap pitch instead of redirecting to curiosity about her specific numbers — this is scripted but leans toward over-explaining rather than pulling her toward her own bill.
alternative_hypothesis: This is the standard, sanctioned explanation for the bill-swap program and answering the direct question is reasonable setter-scope content, not scope creep.
coaching_implication: Minor — the explanation is short and doesn't cross into technical/financial specifics, so this is more a note than a hard miss. No major action needed.

stewart_read: Customer volunteers her bill amount unprompted while pulling up the bill; the rep never reflects it back or uses it as leverage — he moves straight to asking about the graph.
coaching_implication: This is the single clearest missed bill-flip in the call. Coach: even a one-line 'wow, $214 in January — that's a lot for winter, this is exactly the kind of bill the program targets' would have anchored the appointment's value.

quote: Okay. And you're in a what part of Oregon?
stewart_read: Customer questions the rep's location/area code discrepancy, an unmapped legitimacy check not covered by protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number (which addresses contact-info sourcing, not caller-ID/location mismatch). Rep deflects with a vague 'We got a team in Portland' without addressing why his info doesn't show Oregon.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have handled this as well as reasonably possible given a genuinely tangential customer question that doesn't threaten the booking.
coaching_implication: Flag for schema gap: Ion doesn't yet have a scripted response for caller-ID/area-code legitimacy questions distinct from 'how did you get my number.' Until Kenny defines one, coach reps to give a clear, specific answer (state, office, or team name) rather than a vague deflection.

stewart_read: Major vulnerability disclosure met with a brief, low-specificity response before moving back to procedure.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did acknowledge it ('Yeah. I'm sorry.') rather than ignoring it outright, so this is a partial miss, not a total one.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause longer on disclosures like this — even one more sentence of acknowledgment before returning to the ownership/title logistics would land better, per the schema's 'trust gift, not an interruption' framing.

quote: I'm multitasking and feeding my dog.
stewart_read: Rep volunteers an unprompted personal distraction admission mid-call while trying to find a calendar slot, right after fumbling through scheduling logistics — a professionalism lapse that risks customer confidence even though she brushes it off warmly.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer responds warmly ('Oh, you're totally fine'), suggesting rapport was strong enough to absorb it without damage — this could read as harmless candor rather than a real lapse.
coaching_implication: Flag directly with the rep: even when a customer is gracious about it, volunteering mid-call distractions undermines perceived professionalism and should be avoided, especially during the booking sequence.

quote: I'll be here for the rest of my life, probably.
stewart_read: Customer confirms long planned tenure at the property ("probably" retirement/forever home) plus mentions a hobby ranch with horses — both signal a strong long-term-value lead the rep never anchors on.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect long-tenure statements back as a value point ("that's great — long-term ownership is exactly where solar pays off most") rather than letting it pass silently into the next topic.
